chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from al-Kinanī, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Qādhif (one who gives evidence of fornication) if he contradicts himself and repents, is his testimony accepted? He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.أَكْذَبَ نَفْسَهُ: Contradicted himself / denied his own statement
key_terms.الْقَاذِفِ: The one who gives testimony of fornication (shahadah al-zina)

ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of a Qādhif accepted if he repents?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the acceptance of the Qādhif’s testimony upon repentance highlights the principle that sincere tawbah restores a person's legal standing (‘adālah) even after a major sin. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it demonstrates the flexibility of evidentiary rules, prioritizing the purity of the witness’s current state over the permanence of their previous fault. It reflects the broader Shia emphasis on the transformative power of repentance in restoring social and legal rights.
